issues.body: `_model_container_binds` extracts only lines matching `type=bind,[^"]*`. Docker also accepts bind mounts as `--volume host:container` or `-v host:container`. Adding `--volume "$SCRIPT_DIR/..:/registry"` to the existing `container` array mounts the writable registry checkout into the model, yet `_model_container_binds` still prints the same four expected records and the `container+=(` count remains one, so every new #300 containment row stays green. The model can then rewrite the registry script that the later PAT-bearing write-back step executes. Thus the asserted exact filesystem view is not exact and the headline PAT containment can fail silently.
issues.fix_hint: Reject every unrecognized Docker mount/volume form in the launcher, or structurally parse and normalize both `--mount` and `--volume`/`-v` arguments before comparing the complete set. Add a non-crashing mutant that inserts a writable registry checkout with `--volume` (and preferably short `-v`) and require the containment assertion to catch it. Keep the expected mount set independent of the extractor.
issues.title: Exact mount-set assertion ignores Docker volume bind syntax

verdict.summary: The round-1 blocker is fixed: `_pat_binding_scopes` distinguishes step scope from outer YAML scope, and the added job-level and `$GITHUB_ENV` mutants demonstrate that those unsafe early bindings are refused. However, the other half of the headline containment remains unsound. `_model_container_binds` calls its result the model's exact filesystem view but recognizes only Docker `--mount` arguments containing `type=bind`; an ordinary `--volume`/`-v` bind can expose the registry checkout without changing any asserted output or the indirect-append count. Because that checkout is later executed with `REGISTRY_SECRETS_PAT`, this bypass defeats the trust property the new check is meant to enforce. A new blocker remains, so under the required round-comparison scale progress is regressing.
